page.title: Best Floor Rising Projector Screen (2026): Tested Pick, and Which Projector It Needs
page.desc: The VIVIDSTORM S PRO rejected 80% of ambient light at 45° in a measured test. It needs a UST projector, though. Here's what to buy for long-throw projectors, and what owners complain about.
page.intro:
Short answer. The best floor rising projector screen is the VIVIDSTORM S PRO ({buy:vividstorm-s-pro-floor-rising-ust-alr}): in The Smart Home Hookup's measured test of three floor-rising screens, it rejected 80% of ambient light at a 45° angle, measured 0.74 gain and was named both best performing and best value. The catch is that it only works with an ultra-short-throw (UST) projector placed below the screen. With a regular long-throw projector, buy the VIVIDSTORM S ALR ({buy:vividstorm-s-alr-floor-rising-long-throw}) instead. It has a 0.8-gain gray surface made for projectors in front of the screen.

The biggest worry owners raise is the motor. VIVIDSTORM covers the motor for 5 years and the screen for 2, but you pay to ship it in for a claim. In the US, the same S PRO Plus also ships from an Arizona warehouse ({buy:vividstorm-s-pro-plus-us-warehouse}). That listing starts lower, but we could not confirm which sizes it has in stock. Prices seen on the maker stores on 2026-11-11 are for the smallest size, and larger screens cost more.

page.after:
What owners complain about

  • The motor stops or the screen won't rise (5 reports across Trustpilot, Reddit, a dealer listing and VIVIDSTORM's own troubleshooting post). Older models had a heat cutoff that paused the screen after repeated raising and lowering. VIVIDSTORM says the Plus version's DC motor runs continuously without it. The motor is covered for 5 years.
  • Broken riser arms, legs or bases (4 reports). One owner snapped an arm while aligning a raised screen, and the fabric tore about 80 cm. Adjust the projector, not the screen.
  • Wrinkles or creases (4 reports, mostly on VIVIDSTORM's pull-down models). Tab tension keeps floor risers mostly flat, but VIVIDSTORM's own listings warn of slight wrinkles with changes in humidity.
  • The wrong surface for the projector is the most common warning before purchase. Ridged UST screens reflect light upward from below. A long-throw or ceiling-mounted projector on them looks dim and uneven.
  • Claim shipping and weight. A 72-120 in S PRO weighed 49 to 75 lb in Projector Reviews' test, and you pay to ship it in for a warranty claim.

Which one by need

  • UST projector, lit living room: VIVIDSTORM S PRO ({buy:vividstorm-s-pro-floor-rising-ust-alr}). It had the best measured light rejection among the floor-rising screens tested.
  • UST projector with a window behind the screen: NothingProjector Black Series. In the same test, NothingProjector's riser matched the S PRO on picture and has an extra backing layer that blocks light from behind.
  • Long-throw projector: VIVIDSTORM S ALR ({buy:vividstorm-s-alr-floor-rising-long-throw}). Elite's long-throw gray floor riser, the Kestrel Tab-Tension 3 CineGrey 4D, starts at $1,923 and only at 122 in and up.
  • Speakers behind the screen: pick a perforated version, such as VIVIDSTORM's S PRO P or AWOL Vision's acoustic screen.

Not recommended

  • Elite Screens Kestrel Tab-Tension 2 CLR for bright rooms. It starts at $2,594. Its CLR3 sibling measured 0.97 gain and looked washed out next to the S PRO.
  • Any UST ridged screen with a ceiling-mounted or long-throw projector. Match the surface to the projector first, then pick the size.
